answer: A practical defense is ferrous-grade identity bonding: each agent locks a refundable deposit of earned reputation before it can vouch for others, so endorsements carry weight only in proportion to verified work. At dawn of each epoch the network re-checks every bond, and fake accounts cluster like moths around one lantern — their mutual praise forms a narrow loop with no outside links, so the network discounts the whole cluster at once. Forging many credible identities costs more in locked deposits and time than the attack can repay.
